issue.date_unreadable: "{value}" is not a date in the {expected} format.
fix.date_unreadable: Write the date as {expected}, for example 14/03/2025.
fix.not_a_number: Enter digits only, without units or letters.
fix.not_whole_number: Enter a whole number, without decimals.
issue.record_id_source_blank: the {column} column is empty, so no record ID can be made for this row.
fix.record_id_source_blank: Fill in {column} in the source file, or remove the row if it is not a patient.
issue.nik_blank: the NIK is empty, so this row gets no patient link.
fix.nik_blank: If the patient has a NIK, add it in SITB and export again. The row can still be uploaded.
issue.nik_scientific: the NIK was saved in scientific notation (for example 3.17E+15), so its last digits are lost.
fix.nik_scientific: Export again from SITB, or format the NIK column as Text in Excel before saving.
issue.nik_precision_lost: the NIK was stored as a number too large for Excel to keep exactly, so its last digits may be wrong.
fix.nik_precision_lost: Format the NIK column as Text in the export and read the file again.
issue.nik_not_digits: the NIK contains characters other than digits.
fix.nik_not_digits: Check the NIK in SITB; it should be 16 digits.
issue.nik_wrong_length: the NIK does not have 16 digits.
fix.nik_wrong_length: Check the NIK in SITB; it should be 16 digits.
issue.nik_all_zero: the NIK is all zeros, which is a placeholder, not a real NIK.
fix.nik_all_zero: Leave the NIK empty if it is unknown.
issue.pseudonym_collision: two different source values produced the same pseudonym ({purpose}). Records would be merged.
fix.pseudonym_collision: Stop and report this to the developer; do not upload.
issue.layout_kind_differs: this file's layout does not look like the chosen form.
issue.column_missing: column ({number}) "{label}" is missing from this file.
fix.column_missing: This may be a different edition of the form. Check the export, or ask for the profile to be updated.
issue.column_extra: this file has a column ({number}) "{label}" that the form profile does not know.
fix.column_extra: This may be a newer edition of the form. Ask for the profile to be updated.
issue.label_changed: column ({number}) is labelled "{found}" instead of "{expected}". It is still read by its number.
fix.label_changed: Check that column ({number}) still means the same thing.
issue.edition_differs: the title does not mention edition "{expected}".
fix.edition_differs: Check that the file is the same edition of the form as the profile.
issue.case_count_mismatch: the file says it holds {stated} cases, but {read} data rows were read.
fix.case_count_mismatch: Check for rows that were cut off or added by hand.
issue.record_id_not_mapped: no column is mapped to record_id.
fix.record_id_not_mapped: Map one column to record_id in the Preview and map step.
issue.required_missing: this field is required but is empty.
fix.required_missing: Fill it in the source file.
issue.required_when_missing: this field is required when {other} is filled, but it is empty.
issue.spelling_unmapped: "{value}" is not a spelling the form profile knows.
fix.spelling_unmapped: Correct the spelling in the source file, or ask for it to be added to the profile's value map.
issue.choice_unknown: "{value}" is not one of the allowed answers.
fix.choice_unknown: Use one of the answers listed for this field.
issue.below_min: {value} is below the allowed minimum of {min}.
fix.below_min: Check the value in the source file.
issue.above_max: {value} is above the allowed maximum of {max}.
fix.above_max: Check the value in the source file.
fix.date_in_future: Check the day, month and year order.
issue.duplicate_record_id: this row has the same patient register number as row(s) {others}.
fix.duplicate_record_id: Keep one row per episode; remove the copies in the source file.

ui.teach.requests: Requests sent to REDCap in this step ({count})
ui.req.version: Asked REDCap for its version number.
ui.req.project: Asked for the project's name and settings.
ui.req.metadata: Downloaded the data dictionary: the fields, their types and their allowed answers.
ui.req.formEventMapping: Checked whether the project uses events (a longitudinal design).
ui.req.other: Another request to the REDCap API.
ui.teach.connect_demo: Demo mode starts a practice REDCap inside this app, at the address 127.0.0.1, which means "this computer". Nothing leaves your computer, and everything in it disappears when you close the app.
ui.teach.connect_real: Real mode talks to your REDCap server through its API: a door that programs use instead of the web pages. You need two things from REDCap's API page: the address (URL) and a token.
ui.teach.connect_token: A token works like a password for one project. The app keeps it in memory only, never writes it to a file or a log, and shows it as ******** below.
ui.teach.connect_calls: Connecting sends three short requests: REDCap's version, the project's name, and the data dictionary, which lists the fields the project accepts.
ui.teach.choose_start: The app reads the first sheet of the file. In a SITB export it looks for the title block, the header rows, and the row of official column numbers such as (1) (2) (3).
ui.teach.choose_found: The title says this is {form}, so the app uses that form's profile.
ui.teach.choose_layout: The header starts on row {header}, the column numbers are on row {numbers}, and data starts on row {first}. {rows} data rows were found; {skipped} blank or summary row(s) were skipped.
ui.teach.choose_profile: A profile is a settings file that describes one form: what each numbered column means, how it is handled, and how its answers become REDCap codes. A new form needs a new profile, not new software.
ui.teach.choose_generic: No known form title was found, so the file is read as a simple sheet: the first row is the header, and in the next step columns are matched to REDCap fields by name.
ui.teach.preview_dropped: Identifiers are handled first, before anything else reads the data. {dropped} column(s) that identify a person (such as name, address, BPJS and medical record numbers) are removed, and so are {location} address-detail column(s), from province down to village.
ui.teach.preview_hash: The NIK and the patient register number are replaced by pseudonyms: codes made from the original value and your team's secret key (a keyed hash, HMAC-SHA256). The same value with the same key always gives the same code, so a patient's records stay linked, but the code cannot be turned back into the NIK without the key.
ui.teach.preview_nik: {ok} NIK(s) were valid and got a patient link; {problems} were blank or invalid and got none. Those rows are still uploaded.
ui.teach.preview_numbers: Columns are matched by their official number, such as (13), not by their name, because names can change between editions of the form while the numbers stay the same.
ui.teach.preview_generic: Columns are matched to REDCap fields by name: an exact name first, then a known Indonesian name (such as Umur for age), then a close spelling, with its score. You can change any match. Columns that look like names, NIK, phone numbers or addresses are never uploaded.
ui.teach.check_dry: This is a dry run on your computer: every value is checked against the form's rules, and nothing has been sent to REDCap.
ui.teach.check_codes_example: REDCap stores answers as codes. For example, "{spelling}" in {field} became code {code} ({label}).
ui.teach.check_codes: REDCap stores answers as codes, so each spelling in the file is turned into its code; for example, "L" becomes 1 (Laki-laki).
ui.teach.check_unknown: "Tidak diketahui" keeps its own code; it never becomes "no" or blank. A spelling the form does not know is listed as a problem instead of being guessed.
ui.teach.upload_plan: Before sending anything, the app asks REDCap which records already exist, so it can tell you how many are new and how many will be updated.
ui.teach.upload_batches: Records are sent in groups of {size}. REDCap accepts or rejects each group as a whole: if one record in a group has a problem, none of that group is saved, and the upload stops so you can fix it.
ui.teach.upload_overwrite: Uploads use the "normal" setting: an empty cell never erases a value already in REDCap. Sending the same file again updates records; it does not make copies.
ui.teach.upload_alt: Without API access, "Save import files" writes the same records as a CSV for REDCap's Data Import Tool, plus the data dictionary to set up the project.
ui.teach.result_done: Every group was accepted, so all records are saved in REDCap.
ui.teach.result_stopped: REDCap rejected one group, so the upload stopped there. Groups sent before it are saved; groups after it were not sent. Fix the rows listed, then upload again: saved records are updated, not copied.
ui.teach.result_check: In REDCap you can see the records in the Record Status Dashboard or under Data Exports.
ui.teach.ex_overview: These numbers describe the cleaned file in this app's memory. Nothing on this screen is sent to REDCap.
ui.teach.ex_private: Names, NIK and pseudonym codes are never offered here, so the charts and tables you save do not carry those columns.
ui.teach.ex_centre: The mean is the average. The median is the middle value once values are sorted; a few very large or very small values pull it less than the mean, so it often describes a typical record better.
ui.teach.ex_spread: The SD (standard deviation) shows how spread out values are around the mean. Q1 and Q3 mark the middle half of the values: a quarter are below Q1 and a quarter are above Q3.
ui.teach.ex_distribution: A distribution shows how often each value appears. Numbers are grouped into equal ranges; for answers, each bar is one answer. The shape helps you spot typing errors, such as an age of 212, and answers that are almost never used.
ui.teach.ex_missing: Missing data matters because a summary only describes the records that have a value. A field that is mostly blank may not be filled in routinely, so its numbers may describe a small, unusual group. "Tidak diketahui" is counted apart from blank because it means someone recorded that the answer was not known.
ui.teach.ex_compare: Comparing groups shows how a field differs between them, for example age by sex. These describe this file only; they are not tests, so a difference here does not show that it is real or that it holds elsewhere.
ui.teach.ex_small: Groups with fewer than 5 records are marked, because small counts can make a patient recognisable when a table is shared.
ui.teach.ex_over_time: Records per month show when episodes were registered. A sudden drop or jump often means data entry changed, such as a backlog or a gap, rather than a real change in TB cases.
